app.name: Kanhe
nav.label: Main
language.label: Language
sign_in.title: Sign in
sign_in.intro: Use the passkey you registered for this console.
enroll.title: Register your passkey
enroll.intro: This link works once. It registers a passkey on this device for this console.
enroll.name: Your name
enroll.name_hint: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes, or underscores.
home.title: Home
things.title: Things
things.hint: This list comes from the console; a thing's page will check its proof in this browser.
error.title: Something went wrong
error.no_passkeys: This browser cannot use passkeys. Try a recent browser, or another device.
error.cancelled: The passkey was not used. Try again when you are ready.
error.address: Passkeys need this console's name: open it at http://localhost (not an IP address).
keys.locked: This console is locked: it signs nothing until it is unlocked.
keys.secret_hint: A passkey that unlocked the console before unlocks it when you sign in.
keys.wrong: That does not unlock the console.
act.label: Act on this {type} record
act.title: Act on a record
act.role_hint: For example: reviewed, approved. Needed to endorse.
approve.title: Confirm with your passkey
approve.intro: This is exactly what will be signed in your name. Nothing is signed until your passkey confirms it.
approve.done: Signed and registered on the ledger as entry {index}.
approve.checked_here: Checked in this browser: these are the bytes your passkey signs.
approve.checked_by_console: This console has no check in the browser: what you see is the console's description.
approve.mismatch: The console's answer does not match what it asked you to sign. Nothing was signed.
approve.prepare_again: This confirmation cannot be used again: go back and prepare it again.
setup.title: Set up your console
setup.intro: Your name (a nickname works) also names your ledger. Your passkey (Touch ID, Windows Hello, a phone, or a security key) is how you sign in and confirm.
sheet.title: Your recovery code
sheet.intro: If you lose your passkey, this code lets you register a new one, and it unlocks the console's keys. Anyone who has it can take over this console: keep it offline, somewhere safe.
sheet.once: The console shows it this once.
sheet.saved: I have printed or saved my recovery code
sheet.needed: Print or save the code first, then tick the box.
backup.title: Where should backups go?
backup.intro: Choose a folder on an external disk, or one that your cloud drive syncs.
backup.folder_hint: A full path. The console makes the folder if it is missing.
recover.title: Recover with your recovery code
recover.intro: Type the code from your recovery sheet, then create a new passkey on this device. The lost passkey stops working.
recover.code_hint: 26 letters and digits; dashes and spaces do not matter.
recover.name: Owner's name (optional)
recover.name_hint: Needed only if this console has more than one owner.
recover.wrong: That is not this console's recovery code.
recover.done: Your new passkey is now the only one. The lost one no longer signs in or confirms.
home.locked: The ledger shows here once the console is unlocked.
settings.title: Settings
settings.language_here: This browser's language is chosen at the top of the page.
settings.backup_note: Every day while the console is unlocked, it writes a backup there, sealed so that only your recovery code opens it, and keeps the newest seven and one a week for four weeks. Keep the code apart from the folder.
settings.read_only: Only an owner or an admin changes these.
settings.keys_state.locked: Locked: the console signs nothing until it is unlocked.
slot.intro: Your passkey does not unlock this console yet. Sign in with it once more, and it will unlock the console after a restart.
register.title: Register a document
register.no_kinds: There is no kind of document yet.
register.private_hint: Private: only its commitment is on the ledger, until you disclose it.
register.public_hint: Public: anyone who reads the ledger sees it.
register.files_kept: Kept with the record, sealed; the ledger holds only their commitments. 16 MiB a file at most.
register.files_not_kept: The ledger holds only their commitments: keep the files yourself.
kinds.title: Kinds
kinds.hint: A kind is this console's form for a kind of document: its fields and its files. The ledger keeps the documents, not the forms.
kinds.name: Name
kinds.type_hint: How the ledger names its records. Change it only if you have a reason.
kinds.keep: Keep the files with the record, sealed
thing.private_hidden: Hidden from you: only those allowed see a document's private data.
thing.private_locked: Unlock the console to see them.
thing.private_elsewhere: This console does not hold the document's private data.
thing.not_kept: not kept: its owner has it
share.title: Share proof
share.intro: The proof is a file anyone can check without trusting this console. It shows the document's history; private fields stay hidden unless you disclose them.
share.nothing_private: No private fields can be disclosed from here.
share.files: Let it check the files (send the files along)
share.send: Send the proof file to whoever checks it. They verify it in the Verify screen, in the standalone verifier page, or with kanhe verify.
share.send_files: Send the proof file and the files to whoever checks them. They verify them in the Verify screen, in the standalone verifier page, or with kanhe verify.
verify.link: Check a proof someone sent you
verify.title: Verify a proof
verify.intro: Checked in this browser, with the same verifier as kanhe verify: nothing is sent anywhere.
verify.drop: Drop the proof file here, with the files it covers.
verify.ledger_hint: From whoever issued it: without it, the report cannot say whose ledger this is.
verify.unavailable: This console has no verifier in the browser. Use the standalone verifier page, or kanhe verify.
verify.verified: Every signature, receipt, and commitment checks, and it comes from the ledger you named.
verify.unconfirmed: Every signature, receipt, and commitment checks. Give the expected ledger id to confirm who issued it.
verify.mismatch: A file is not the one the document committed to.
verify.complete: Complete: the ledger's state proves nothing was left out.
verify.incomplete: The checkpoint cannot prove that nothing, such as a later revocation, was left out.
column.name: Name
approve.name: Name
rules.title: Rules
rules.hint: Rules are the contracts on this ledger: what may happen to a thing, who starts it, and whose consent it needs. The ledger runs them the same way for everyone, and anyone can check that it did.
rules.retire_intro: Retired rules put no new thing under them. Things already under them carry on by the same rules.
rules.retire_reason_hint: Kept on the ledger with the retirement.
rules.read_only: Only an owner or an admin writes rules.
rules.no_compiler: This console was built without the Bo compiler, so it cannot write rules here. Use bo build and kanhe contract deploy.
rules.editor_intro: Fill in the form, or write the Bo text: they are two views of the same rules. Check them, read them as a contract in three languages, run their tests, then deploy them with your passkey.
rules.open_hint: A Bo source (.bo) or a rules sheet (.json), such as one of the examples. A source that fits the form opens in it.
rules.unfit: These rules do not fit the form, so they stay as text: {reason}
rules.source_hint: One clause a line; a block indented by two spaces. Keywords in any of the three languages.
rules.packs_hint: Words for a field of work. A pack's words mean something only when its box is ticked.
rules.explain_hint: Bo wrote these texts from the rules, and each says the same.
rules.no_tests: These rules have no tests yet: add them under Tests in the form.
rules.sheet.contract.hint: The contract's name, such as Lending.
rules.sheet.parties.hint: The roles in these rules, such as owner. Each is a ledger of its own once a thing is created.
rules.sheet.actions.hint: What may happen to the thing, and who starts it.
rules.sheet.rules.hint: What happens by itself when a time comes.
rules.sheet.answers.hint: What happens when a request is done, fails, or expires.
rules.sheet.tests.hint: Each test runs its steps on a thing of its own, every party a ledger of its own.
rules.thing.word.hint: thing, unless a pack you use has a word of its own.
rules.thing.name: Name of the kind
rules.thing.name.hint: Such as Item. Leave it empty for rules without fields.
rules.field.name: Name
rules.field.type.hint: Such as text, number, date, HKD, or a party: the field then holds that party.
rules.action.by.hint: A party, or a field that holds one.
rules.action.to.hint: The other party, such as counterparty.
rules.action.requires.hint: Each must hold, or the call is refused.
rules.action.in_person_over.hint: Such as over 5000: only above it is a person's passkey needed.
rules.action.agents_propose: AI agents may only propose it
rules.input.name: Name
rules.assign.name: Name
rules.rule.when.hint: A time, such as suspended 30 days: a state held that long.
rules.test.name: Name (optional)
rules.test.name.hint: A text in quotes, such as "shared, then closed".
rules.step.args.hint: Such as at 2027-01-05, or in person.
rules.step.expect.hint: Such as a state, consent of friend1, or refused "why".
thing.create_intro: Fill in what the rules ask for. Prepare runs the creation as the ledger will; then your passkey confirms it.
thing.what_it_does: What the contract says of it
thing.no_calls: This console cannot show what these rules take: they are not written in Bo, or this console has no compiler.
thing.values_problem: Some values do not fit: see the fields marked.
thing.problem.unknown: The rules take no such value.
thing.problem.literal: Write one value, as in the example.
thing.problem.exact: Finer than its smallest unit, or too large.
thing.problem.ledger: A ledger id is 64 hexadecimal digits.
thing.problem.bound: Too many items for this list.
thing.problem.function: The rules have no such call.
thing.needs_consent: This needs the consent of another ledger ({ledgers}), given on that ledger: ask for it below.
thing.title: A thing under rules
thing.actions_hint: Prepare runs the call as the ledger will and shows what it decides; nothing is signed until your passkey confirms it.
thing.requests_hint: Requests the rules made for work outside the ledger. An executor answers them, or you do by hand.
thing.answer_reason_hint: For a failure: a code such as cancelled or unavailable.
thing.share_intro: The proof is a file with every call on this thing: anyone checks it without trusting this console.
exchange.note_hint: Shown to whoever reads the proposal; at most 1000 bytes.
exchange.ask_intro: Write a proposal file and send it to the other party by any channel. They consent on their own ledger and send back a consent file, which you open here to record the call.
exchange.proposal_made: Saved {name}. Send it to the other party; when their consent file comes back, open it from Home.
exchange.title: Proposals and consents
exchange.intro: Open a proposal or consent file someone sent you. It is verified here before you do anything with it.
exchange.verified: Verified: the thing's history checks for the ledger that sent it, and the call is the one it names.
exchange.not_asked: The proposal does not ask this ledger for its consent.
exchange.consent_intro: Your consent names this one call at the thing's current step, and counts once. After the tap, a consent file is saved: send it back.
exchange.consent_made: Saved {name}. Send it back to whoever sent the proposal.
exchange.consent_verified: Verified on the consenting ledger: its terms are this call's.
exchange.not_ours: This consent is to a call on another ledger's thing.
exchange.lapsed: This consent has lapsed: ask again.
exchange.moved_on: The thing has moved on since this consent: ask again.
exchange.record: Record the call with your passkey
exchange.record_intro: The call runs with the consent first, as the ledger will run it.
exchange.link: Open a proposal or consent file
exchange.proposed: This ledger's registrar holds the call until {until}, and records it as soon as the consents come in online.
exchange.no_registrar: This console runs no registrar: ask by file instead.
parties.title: Parties
parties.intro: Other ledgers this console works with: each connected with one code each way. Once connected, calls that wait for your consent on their ledgers show on Home, and your consent goes back online; you ask each other for documents; and each witnesses the other's ledger, cosigning only checkpoints that extend what it cosigned before.
parties.our_fingerprint: This ledger's fingerprint, to compare by voice: {fingerprint}
parties.name: Their name here
parties.name_hint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores: such as bob.
parties.accept_name_hint: The name you invited them with, if you did.
parties.code_secret: Send it to that party only: it holds the token they call this ledger's API with. Compare fingerprints by voice: {fingerprint}
parties.accepted: Connected with {name}: {organization}, fingerprint {fingerprint}. Compare it with them by voice.
parties.reply_for: Send this code back to {name}, so that they connect with you too:
parties.sent_recorded: Sent to {name}: the call is recorded on their ledger.
parties.sent_waiting: Sent to {name}: the call still waits for other consents.
access.accept_hint: Accepting records a receipt on this ledger and sends it to them.
access.ask_intro: Ask a party reached online for one of its documents. They choose what to share; it comes sealed to this ledger.
access.cannot_grant: You cannot share this document from here: it is not yours to share, or its private data is not here.
access.dismissed: Dismissed: it is no longer asked of you.
access.document_hint: The document's full id, as the party gave it (on a proof they shared, say).
access.fields_hint: Names separated by commas; leave empty to ask for all.
access.grant_days_hint: 1 to 366, and never past the end they asked for.
access.granted_already: You granted this already; granting again replaces the delivery.
access.missing: This document is not on this ledger, or was revoked.
access.not_verified: This delivery does not check out: {message}
access.sent: Sent to {peer}. It shows on Home once they share it.
access.unreadable: This request does not check out: {message}
access.verified: Verified: {by} granted it on {organization}'s ledger, and the document checks against that ledger.
access.answered_ok: Answered: {peer} fetches the answer from here.
access.question_intro: Ask a party reached online whether conditions hold in one of its documents. They answer with a claim checked against the document: you learn whether it holds, never the fields.
access.question_days_hint: How long the question stays open: 1 to 366 days.
access.answered_already: You answered this already; answering again replaces the answer kept for them.
access.replaced: The document has a newer version: answer on the latest one, or dismiss the question.
access.cannot_answer: You cannot answer for this document from here: it is not yours to read, or its private data is not here.
access.holds_now: As the document stands, this holds.
access.does_not_hold_now: As the document stands, this does not hold. Nothing is answered unless you choose to answer that it does not; to them, dismissing it looks the same as silence.
access.answer_intro: Your answer is a claim on this ledger: the condition and whether it holds, never the fields. They fetch it from here.
access.answer_no: Answer that it does not hold
access.says_not: Verified: {organization} says that it does not hold that {condition}.
access.question_sent: Sent to {peer}. Their answer shows on Home once they give it.
access.by_console: This console answers by itself the questions each kind allows, when they hold, signed by its machine; the others wait for you.
access.allow_console: Let the console answer by itself
access.allow_console_hint: Kinds can let the console answer questions about some of their fields. Once you allow it with your passkey, the console's machine answers those that hold; the others wait for a person.
parties.refused: This console refused to cosign {name}'s ledger: {message}. A ledger that does not extend what was cosigned before may have been rewritten, or shown differently to different parties: ask them.
parties.not_cosigned: {name} has not cosigned this ledger's latest checkpoint: {message}
people.title: People
people.intro: Who uses this console, with which role, and what each may do on the ledger. Roles decide what they see and manage here; what they may do on the ledger is a delegation, which the ledger itself checks, always with their passkey's tap.
people.approve_intro: Choose what they may do on the ledger. Then confirm, with your passkey: their person on the ledger (with a key this console keeps for them), their passkeys, and what they may do, one tap each.
people.approved: {name} may now act on the ledger, each time with their passkey.
people.until_hint: After this day they may do none of it.
people.may.act: create and act on things under rules
people.may.act_rules: create and act on things under {rules}
people.may.people: register people and grant what they may do
people.withdrawn: Withdrawn: {name} may no longer do it on the ledger.
people.removed: {name} no longer uses this console; withdraw what they may do on the ledger too, if they had anything.
people.link_hint: Send it to them only. It registers a passkey on their own device, once, until {time}; then approve them here.
people.new_key: Their key, kept by this console
tokens.title: API tokens
tokens.intro: For programs that use this ledger's API. A token is shown once, when it is made.
tokens.once: Copy it now: it is not shown again.
activity.title: Activity in this console
thing.action_link_hint: Whoever opens it signs in and sees this action's form; it is checked and confirmed as any other, so the link holds no secret. Print the code, or show it for a phone to scan.
thing.action_unavailable: The action {action} is not offered on this thing now (or not to you).
automation.title: Automation
automation.intro: Machines act on the ledger without a person's tap: executors answer the requests rules make, AI agents work for a person who answers for them, and the console's own machine fires time rules while the console is unlocked. Each machine may do only what its delegation says.
automation.keeper_runs: The console's machine fires these while the console is unlocked.
automation.keeper_locked: The console is locked: nothing fires until it is unlocked.
automation.executor_intro: An executor answers the requests of some kinds that one set of rules makes (a notice to send, a bill to raise), through its connectors, and may do nothing else. It runs elsewhere, with a key it is given once.
automation.kinds_hint: Separated by commas, as the rules name them: notify, bill.
automation.functions_hint: Leave empty for the rules' own: result, if they have it.
automation.name_hint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes, underscores; it also names its API token.
automation.no_rules: Deploy rules first: an executor answers the requests of a set of rules.
automation.agent_intro: An AI agent works through the MCP server for a person who answers for it. Its statements are a machine's, never in person, and the evidence shows its model.
automation.model_hint: The model it runs, as its maker names it.
automation.no_people: Approve a person first: an AI agent answers to one.
automation.setup_executor: Its key is handed out now, once: the console does not keep it. Choose a passphrase that encrypts it; the executor needs both.
automation.setup_agent: Its key is handed out now, once: the console does not keep it. Choose a passphrase that encrypts it; the MCP server needs both.
automation.passphrase_hint: At least 8 characters. Keep it with the machine, not here.
automation.once: Shown once: save the key and copy the token now.
automation.connectors_hint: Add its connectors to the config first (kanhe executor connector add), and the token to a file.
automation.mcp_hint: Save the token and the passphrase in the files it names, beside the key.
activity.automation.delegate: granted what a machine may do
approve.by_organization: the organization, with its root key: what a machine may do needs no person's presence, so no person's delegation can grant it. This console checks your passkey, and its activity log keeps who approved it.
home.backup_none: No backup yet: the first comes within the day.
home.backup_no_folder: No backup folder: choose one in Settings, and the console backs up every day.
witnesses.title: Public witnesses
witnesses.intro: A public witness cosigns this ledger's checkpoints, so that anyone can tell its history was never rewritten. It learns the ledger's id, its first keys, each checkpoint's size, root, and time, and this computer's address; never statements, records, fields, parties, or files.
witnesses.stopped: {name} is no longer asked. What it cosigned stays valid.
witnesses.key_hint: As its operator publishes it. Check it with them: a witness's own page cannot vouch for itself.
witnesses.add: Ask it to witness this ledger
witnesses.added: {name} cosigned this ledger at {size} entries, and will be asked after each new checkpoint.
activity.witnesses.add: asked a public witness to witness this ledger
relay.title: Reached through a relay
relay.intro: A console on a laptop is reached by its parties through a relay: the server of a public witness it asks. Their requests wait there, sealed for this console, until it fetches and answers them. The relay learns who writes to whom and when, never what.
relay.direct: Parties reach this console directly, at its own address.
relay.used: Parties now reach this console through {name}. Give them a new invitation code.
relay.none_possible: Add a public witness first: its server can be this console's relay.
relay.stopped: Parties reach this console directly again. New invitation codes carry no relay.
relay.problem: The relay could not be reached: {message}
activity.relay.use: chose a relay for parties to reach this console
activity.certificates.allow: let the console issue a kind's certificates
activity.certificates.credential: issued a certificate as a W3C credential
activity.credentials.allow: let the console's credential key issue credentials
activity.answers.allow: let the console answer questions by itself
activity.access.answered: answered a party's question by itself
thing.superseded: A newer version replaced this document (entry {index}). Use the latest version.
register.replaces_hint: This is a new version of {name} ({id}). Once you confirm it, anyone who checks the old one is told a newer version replaced it.
search.hint: Searches look at what the ledger holds in the clear: kinds, states, times, and public information. Private fields are never searched; they stay sealed.
report.title: Reports
report.hint: Counts of what the ledger holds, from its search index. Days are in this browser's time ({offset}).
report.unavailable: This console's node keeps no search index, so it has no reports.
report.sum_hint: The field's name in the rules, such as total or fee.
report.truncated: Only the first 10,000 groups are shown.
kinds.answers: The console may answer questions about it
certificates.title: Certificates
certificates.intro: Each certificate carries a QR code that opens it as it is now: whoever scans it sees whether it is genuine, revoked, or replaced, who issued it and when, and the fields printed on it, nothing else.
certificates.unreachable: Scanners would reach these certificates at {address}, which only this computer opens. Run the console at a public address (kanhe-console run --public-url) before printing them.
certificates.no_kinds: No kind prints fields yet. In Kinds, mark the fields a new kind prints on its certificates.
certificates.allowed_not_yet: not yet: an owner allows it
certificates.allowed: The console may now issue {name} certificates.
certificates.qr_alt: QR code that opens the certificate of {what}
certificates.link_label: The link the QR code of {what} holds
certificates.withdrawn: The certificate of {what} is taken down: its QR code finds nothing now. Its record stays on the ledger; revoke it to say it no longer stands.
certificates.issue_intro: A spreadsheet saved as CSV (UTF-8): a first line naming the kind's fields, then a row per certificate. Once you confirm the batch with your passkey, the console's machine signs each one: the ledger shows them as issued by the organization's device.
certificates.none_allowed: An owner first lets the console issue a kind (above).
certificates.failed: Stopped: {problem}. Issue the same table again to carry on.
credentials.title: In digital wallets
credentials.off_intro: A certificate can also be handed over as a W3C Verifiable Credential, for a digital wallet to hold and any standard verifier to check. The console then gets a key of its own for them, registered on the ledger, which records each credential it issues.
credentials.turned_on: Credentials are on: each valid certificate now downloads as a credential.
credentials.on_intro: Credentials are on. Each valid certificate downloads as a W3C Verifiable Credential (.jwt) issued by {issuer}, whose DID document and status lists this console serves.
credentials.no_issuer: This console's address cannot name an issuer ({problem}): run it at a public https address first.
certificates.credential_label: Download the certificate of {what} as a W3C credential
claim.title: What it confirms
claim.intro: Confirm that a condition on this document's fields holds, without showing them: "monthly_salary is above HKD 30,000.00", not the salary. The console checks it against the document's private data; whoever checks the claim later sees the condition and the answer, and whether the document was revoked or replaced since.
claim.value_hint: Values: money as HKD 30000.00, dates as YYYY-MM-DD, numbers, or text (in quotes if it looks like a number or a date). "is between": LOW and HIGH. "is one of": A, B, C. Several conditions must all hold.
claim.subject: About whom or what
claim.subject_hint: Optional: as the claim names them, such as the person's name.
claim.until_hint: Optional: after this day, whoever checks it sees that it lapsed.
claim.allow_no: If it does not hold, issue a claim that says so (otherwise nothing is issued, which reveals nothing)
claim.status.unknown: the document is not on this ledger
scripts.title: Scripts
scripts.intro: A script is a program whose output becomes records, such as a monthly report or an executor's answers. Approving one puts the digest of each of its files on the ledger, approved in person with your passkey. Records then name the script they came from, and anyone can check its files against the approval. Each new version is approved on its own; a withdrawn script can no longer be named.
scripts.approve_intro: Choose its files, or its folder. This browser computes each file's digest: only their paths, sizes, and digests are sent, never the files. Your passkey then approves it, in person.
scripts.name: Name
scripts.version_hint: Such as 1.0. Each version is approved on its own.
scripts.note_hint: Kept sealed with the approval, as its one private field.
scripts.deterministic_box: Deterministic: the same inputs always give the same output, so that whoever is given them may run it again and compare
scripts.folder_hint: Every file in it, by its path below it; hidden ones (names starting with a dot) are left out.
scripts.files_hint: Each file is named by its path in the script's folder, with its digest under the ledger's hash, {hash}.
scripts.bad_path: {path} cannot name a script's file: it is a path in its folder, without "..".
scripts.no_digest: This browser cannot compute the ledger's hash without the console's checks.
scripts.in_person_passkey: by {name}, in person with a passkey, {time}
scripts.in_person_key: by {name}, in person with a hardware key, {time}
scripts.withdrawn_notice: Withdrawn on {time}: records can no longer name it. Those that named it before keep their history.
scripts.check_intro: Choose the files you have, or their folder: this browser compares their digests with the approval. Nothing is sent.
scripts.check_same: These files are the script as approved.
scripts.check_same_withdrawn: These files are the script as approved, but its approval was withdrawn.
scripts.check_differ: {n} of {of} files differ from the approval.
scripts.withdraw_intro: Records can then no longer name it, and executors set up with it stop running it. Records that named it keep their history, and their proofs say it was withdrawn.
scripts.reason_hint: Optional: why. Kept on the ledger.
made.title: Where it came from
made.stale: A source was revoked or replaced since this record was made. The record stands as it is: whoever relies on it decides what that means.
made.local_line: on this ledger: {then} when this record was made; now {now}
made.remote_line: {type} on {ledger}'s ledger: {then} when this record was made; {now} as of {time}
made.remote_no_proof: a record on {ledger}'s ledger: no proof of it is kept here, so its standing is not shown
made.remote_bad_proof: a record on {ledger}'s ledger: the proof kept here does not hold ({problem})
register.made_from_hint: The records it was made from, and the script that made it. Only their ids go on the ledger, never their fields; its proof then shows whether each is still live.
register.source_ids_hint: 64 hexadecimal digits; read from the proof if you give one.
register.source_proof_hint: The record's evidence, as its ledger gave it (a .cbor file): the console checks it and keeps it with this record, so that this record's proof shows where the source stands.
register.source_ids: Give that ledger's id and the record's id, 64 hexadecimal digits each, or a proof that names them.
register.script_hint: One of the scripts approved on this ledger (Scripts).
verify.script_line: the script {name} {version} ({files} files), approved in person by {person}, {time};
verify.script_deterministic: deterministic: whoever is given its inputs may run it again;

approvals.state.dropped: dropped: the ledger can no longer take it
approve.type.actor-rotate-key: Give an actor a new key
approve.type.ledger-rotate-log-key: Give the ledger a new log key
approve.type.record-transition: Move a record to another state
approve.needs: Others must approve this before it is registered: {rules}.
approve.needs_hint: Once you confirm, it is sent to them and registered the moment enough of them approve. If too few have approved by {time}, it lapses.
approve.note_hint: Up to 1,000 characters. It stays with the request on this console, never on the ledger.
approve.show_fields_hint: So that they see what they approve. The values are kept on this console, readable, until it is registered or lapses, then deleted; the ledger still holds only their sealed commitments.
approve.will_propose: The rules keep this call as a proposal: it takes effect once enough people approve it.
approve.proposed: Kept as a proposal: it takes effect once enough people approve it (Approvals).
approvals.sent_done: It waits for their approvals until {time}. Follow it under Approvals.
approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.intro: What waits for your approval, and what you sent for approval. An approval is your agreement to something someone else signed: the ledger registers it only once enough of the people its rules name approve it, each in person with their passkey.
approvals.no_actor: You act as no one on the ledger yet, so nothing waits for your approval.
approvals.none_sent: You sent nothing for approval in the last 30 days.
approvals.completes: Your approval completes it: the action takes effect at once.
approvals.records: Your approval is recorded; more are needed.
approvals.withdrawn: Withdrawn: this console holds it no more.
approvals.withdraw_hint: Withdrawing it stops this console from registering it. Anyone who keeps a copy with enough approvals could still register it until it lapses.
approvals.review_intro: This is exactly what you are asked to approve. Your approval is signed in your name, in person with your passkey, for this statement alone.
approvals.mismatch: The console's answer does not match the statement's own bytes. Nothing was approved.
approvals.checked_here: Checked in this browser: these are the statement's own bytes, and its id is computed from them.
approvals.fields_shown: Its fields came with it, checked in this browser against what it commits to.
approvals.fields_sealed: Its fields did not come with it: you approve its kind, files, and terms without seeing the values.
approvals.registered: Your approval completed it: registered on the ledger as entry {index}.
approvals.kept: Your approval is kept. It needs more before it is registered.
approvals.declined: Declined: whoever sent it sees that you said no. Nothing goes on the ledger.
approvals.decline_hint: Declining only tells whoever sent it. Not approving is enough to stop it: it lapses if too few approve.
home.approvals_sent: {n} you sent for approval, still waiting
people.approvals_needed: Others must approve what they sign
people.approvals_hint: Then each statement they sign this way is held until enough of the people you choose approve it, each in person with their passkey. They count as one of them if you choose them too.
people.approvals_days_hint: 1 to 30. If too few approve within this time of its preparation, it lapses.
people.approvals_open: Also count approvals that are not in person
people.approvals_open_warning: Not in person means a key alone counts: an AI agent's, a machine's, or a person's without their passkey. Choose it only for automated checks you trust; the proof says each such approval was not in person.
guardians.title: Guardians of the top key
guardians.intro: The organization's top key signs what no one else may: the ledger's new keys, and whatever the organization registers itself. Guardians are people who must approve what it signs, so that a stolen top key alone can do nothing.
guardians.in_effect: The top key is guarded by {k} of {n} guardians: {names} (since entry {index}).
guardians.second_passkey: {names}: fewer than two passkeys. Ask them to register a second passkey, or a hardware key kept apart.
guardians.none: No guardians: the top key signs alone.
guardians.waiting: A change of guardians waits for their approvals.
guardians.k_hint: Choose at least one guardian more than this, so that one lost passkey does not lock the organization.
guardians.within_hint: Days, 1 to 30, from when a statement is prepared.
guardians.warning_lockout: If fewer of them than must approve can ever approve again (people leave, passkeys are lost), what they guard can never be signed again, and the only remedy is a new ledger.
guardians.warning_spare: So name at least one more guardian than must approve.
guardians.warning_passkeys: Ask each guardian to register a second passkey, or a hardware key kept somewhere else.
guardians.warning_work: Day-to-day work does not wait for them: people and this console's machine act under their own delegations. What the organization signs itself does: {work}.
guardians.work.credentials: turning on credentials for digital wallets
guardians.work.certificates: letting the console issue a kind's certificates
guardians.work.answers: letting the console answer questions by itself
guardians.work.recovery: replacing a lost passkey with the recovery code
guardians.no_spare: I accept having no guardian to spare
guardians.remove_hint: Removing them needs the approvals of the current guardians.
rules.action.approvals.hint: Such as: above 1_000_000, 2 approvals by directors, in person, within 7 days. Until then the call is kept as a proposal.
rules.approval.by.hint: A field or input holding a person or a list of people, such as directors. Without it, anyone whom the delegations let approve.
rules.approval.within.hint: Such as within 7 days (1 day to 12 months).
rules.action.agents_approve: AI agents may approve it (where no one must be in person)
activity.approvals.withdraw: withdrew a statement sent for approval
approvals.proposed_by_agent: Proposed by an AI agent: a person must approve it, in person.
approvals.you_count: (you count as one of them, in person)
approvals.machine_continues: Once it is registered, the console grants the machine what you chose by itself (signed by the organization, and sent for approval again if that needs it); then set it up from Automation.
approvals.steps_wait: The next steps wait for it: take them once it is registered.
automation.set_up_hint: Their registration and what they may do are on the ledger now: take each key once, as when adding it.
recover.held_then: Your new passkey works once enough of them have approved it, by {time}. Until then it does not sign in, and the lost one is still the one on the ledger. They see it under Approvals.
activity.recovery.held: sent a lost passkey's recovery for approval
setup.long_term: Will these records need to verify in 20 years or more? (certificates, diplomas, deeds, contracts)
setup.long_term_hint: A future quantum computer could forge the signatures in use today. Post-quantum keys stay safe, so with them these records stay verifiable for decades; the console calls them long-term keys. With today's keys, you can prepare for the long term later in Settings.
home.long_term: These records rely on signatures a future quantum computer could forge: prepare for the long term before 2030.
home.certificate_expiring: The time-stamp authority {authority}'s certificate expires on {date}, in {days} days: what to do
home.certificate_expired: The time-stamp authority {authority}'s certificate expired on {date}: what to do
long_term.title: Keep records verifiable for decades
long_term.intro: A future quantum computer could forge the signatures most systems use today. Post-quantum keys stay safe: records signed with them stay verifiable for decades. Here they are called long-term keys.
long_term.born: This ledger began with long-term keys: its records stay verifiable for decades.
long_term.converted: This ledger's keys are long-term keys now. It began with today's keys, so its earlier records rely on a witness that cosigned with a long-term key.
long_term.classical: This ledger signs with today's keys (top key {root}, log key {log}), which a quantum computer could forge. Prepare for the long term before 2030.
long_term.witness_none: None yet: ask a witness whose key is long-term (Parties, Public witnesses)
long_term.certificate: The time-stamp authority {authority}'s certificate expires on {date}, in {days} days: check that it has a new one, or use another authority.
long_term.certificate_expired: The time-stamp authority {authority}'s certificate expired on {date}: use an authority whose certificate is current.
long_term.step.rotate-log-key: Give the ledger a long-term log key
long_term.step.rotate-root-key: Give the organization a long-term top key
long_term.step.checkpoint: Sign a checkpoint with the new log key
long_term.prepare_hint: You confirm each new key with your passkey. The console makes the new keys, keeps them where it keeps today's, and then signs a checkpoint with the new log key. People, documents, and rules stay as they are.
long_term.guardians_hint: Your guardians approve each new key before it takes effect. Once they have approved one, the console takes the next step by itself.
long_term.why_not.owner: Only an owner prepares the ledger for the long term.
long_term.why_not.locked: The console is locked: unlock it first.
long_term.why_not.held: A new key waits for the guardians' approval.
long_term.why_not.root: This console does not keep the organization's top key: prepare the ledger with kanhe ledger long-term on the command line.
long_term.why_not.restart: Restart the console first (kanhe-console stop, then kanhe-console open), so that it holds the new log key ready.
long_term.renew_old: Proof files given out before the change can be renewed, so that a long-term signature covers them:
long_term.done: Done: the ledger's keys are long-term keys, and a checkpoint is signed with the new log key.
long_term.checkpoint_made: A checkpoint is signed with the log key in effect.
long_term.continues: Once it is registered, the console takes the next step by itself (signed by the organization, and sent for approval again if that needs it).
long_term.proof_safe: Stays verifiable for decades: a long-term signature covers it ({who}, at {size} entries).
long_term.proof_not_yet: No long-term signature covers it yet: renew it before {date}, once a witness has cosigned with a long-term key.
renew.title: Renew a proof file
renew.intro: Someone brings back a proof file this ledger made: renewing adds the ledger's newest checkpoint that a witness cosigned or a time-stamp authority stamped, so that it stays verifiable for longer. Nothing in it changes, and nothing private is added.
renew.done: Renewed: saved {name}, now up to the checkpoint of {size} entries ({time}).
renew.send: Give the renewed file back to whoever brought it: it replaces the old one.
renew.other_ledger: This proof file comes from another ledger: only that ledger can renew it.
renew.not_attested: No witness has cosigned, and no time-stamp authority has stamped, a checkpoint since this proof file was made. Ask a witness (Parties, Public witnesses), then try again.
renew.not_a_proof: This is not a document's proof file.
renew.nothing_new: This proof file has the newest attested checkpoint already: there is nothing to add yet.
activity.long-term.log-key: gave the ledger a long-term log key
activity.long-term.root-key: gave the organization a long-term top key
activity.long-term.checkpoint: signed a checkpoint with the new log key
long_term.signer: the organization, with its top key in effect, as every new key of the ledger is signed. This console checks your passkey, and its activity log keeps who confirmed it.
ranges.title: Values that can be proven without showing them
ranges.provable_line: Can be proven without showing the value: {list}.
ranges.provable_fact: Can be proven later without showing the value
ranges.issuers_word: That each of these is the document's own value is the issuer's word, signed when it was registered.
ranges.thing_hint: A proof shows only the statement, such as that a value is at least an amount, never the value itself.
ranges.enc_money_0: an amount in {currency}, in whole units
ranges.enc_money_1: an amount in {currency} with 1 decimal place
ranges.enc_money: an amount in {currency} with {scale} decimal places
ranges.not_checked: not checked: this verifier cannot check proofs of this kind, so nothing rests on it
ranges.none: This file carries no proof of them.
ranges.none_for_challenge: This file carries no range proof, so it proves no range, and your challenge code was not used.
verify.challenge_hint: A fresh code you gave whoever proves: every range proof must then carry it, which shows it was made after you asked, not copied from an older proof.
verify.challenge_bad: A challenge code is 2 to 128 hex digits (0-9 and a-f), an even number of them.
verify.challenge_failed: Not verified with your challenge code
verify.challenge_failed_detail: Without the code this proof file verifies, but a range proof in it does not carry your code: it may have been made before you asked, or for someone else. Ask for a new one.
renew.range_proofs: The values it proves without showing them still hold:
kinds.provable: Can be proven later without showing the value
kinds.provable_currency_label: Currency, for an amount of money (optional)
kinds.provable_mark: , can be proven later without showing it ({encoding})
register.provable_hint: Can be proven later without showing it ({encoding}): that it is at least, at most, or between values you choose.
prove.title: Prove a range
prove.intro: Prove that a value is at least, at most, or between values you choose, without showing the value. The proof file shows only that statement; anyone can check it without trusting this console.
prove.number_hint: Write it as a number, with at most {scale} decimal places, such as 18 or 60.5.
prove.money_hint: An amount in {currency}, with at most {scale} decimal places, such as 30000 or {currency} 30,000.00.
prove.challenge_hint: If they gave you a code, enter it: the proof then carries it, which shows them it was made for their request.
prove.nothing: Choose what to prove of at least one value.
prove.working: Making the proof: this may take a few seconds...
prove.done: Saved {name}, checked before it was offered. It proves:
prove.send: Send the proof file to whoever asked. They check it in their Verify screen, in the standalone verifier page, or with kanhe verify.
prove.send_challenge: Send the proof file to whoever gave you the challenge code. They check it with the same code, in their Verify screen, in the standalone verifier page, or with kanhe verify.
prove.not_within: The value is not within those bounds, so no proof of it can be made.
prove.bad_challenge: A challenge code is 2 to 128 hex digits (0-9 and a-f), an even number of them.
prove.no_provable: This document has no values that can be proven: its kind marked none when it was registered.
prove.unsupported: This console was built without range proofs, so it cannot make them.
openings.title: Let the holder prove
openings.intro: The person these values belong to can prove them by themselves, as often as they like, with the document's proof file and a values file from you. Their own tools check the values file against this document first.
openings.warning_title: This file holds the values themselves
openings.warning: Whoever has it learns the values and can prove them. Give it only to the person they belong to, privately: never by a public link, and never to the one who checks the proof.
openings.understood: I will give it only to the person these values belong to
openings.confirm_first: Confirm first that you will give it only to the person these values belong to.
openings.then: Give it to the person, with the document's proof file (Share proof). With kanhe evidence prove they make proofs from it.
activity.record.openings: gave out a document's values file
activity.evidence.prove: proved a document's value within bounds
archives.title: Archives that keep this ledger
archives.intro: An archive is a trust node that keeps a read-only copy of this ledger and the evidence of each certificate it publishes, and answers for them if this ledger's own server closes. Its operator gives you its address.
archives.token: The archive copies this ledger with a token whose only scope is an archive: make one under People, API tokens, and give it to the archive's operator with this ledger's address.
archives.hint: Links printed after you add an archive name it, so those certificates still verify if this ledger's server closes. Links printed before do not.
archives.checking: Asking each archive for its latest copy...
archives.none: No archive keeps this ledger yet.
archives.problem.not_checkpoint: Its answer is not a checkpoint.
archives.problem.other_ledger: It keeps another ledger at this address.
archives.problem.not_ours: It answered a checkpoint this ledger never made.
archives.removed: New links no longer name the archive {url}. Links printed before still do.
archives.url_hint: For example https://trust.example.org, or its address for this ledger, which ends in /a/{ledger}
archives.added: The archive at {url} keeps this ledger: its latest copy has {size} entries. Certificates' links name it from now on.
archives.full: This ledger lists {max} archives, the most a link names. Remove one to add another.
archives.damaged: The list of archives cannot be read: {message}
archives.refused.not_address: That is not an archive's address for this ledger: give the archive's server (https://HOST), or its address for this ledger, which ends in /a/{ledger}.
archives.refused.listed: This ledger lists that archive already.
archives.refused.full: This ledger lists four archives already, the most a link names.
archives.refused.too_long: With that address, a certificate's link would be too long for its QR code to stay readable. Use an archive with a shorter address.
archives.refused.unreachable: The archive did not answer, so it was not added ({message}).
archives.refused.not_checkpoint: The archive's answer is not a checkpoint, so it was not added.
archives.refused.other_ledger: That archive keeps another ledger at this address, so it was not added.
archives.refused.not_ours: That archive answered a checkpoint this ledger never made, so it was not added.
activity.archives.add: added an archive that keeps this ledger
